solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gesture when in male corner

indicators.note: the word for 'when' is placed in the gap between the male bird and the corner

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
a nook is a corner
'as' can mean 'when' (as I left = when I left)

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a corner with a man makes a rude gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal: the word for 'when' sits in the gap between the two other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Thumbing one's nose, thumb on nose and fingers spread, is the classic derisive gesture this phrase names.

clue.text: Split from extremely clever First Lady hiding fool

indicators.note: extremely means the extremes, the first and last letters, of clever
the First Lady hides the fool inside her name

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A president's wife breaks with a very bright partner over concealing an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's wife; it is Eve, the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep crack in a glacier is a split in the ice.

clue.text: American escaping from even church's grasp

indicators.note: the American letter escapes from the word, leaving it

parts.note: clean can mean even, smooth or regular, as in a clean edge
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: An American breaks free from the firm grip of a level-headed church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even' looks like an intensifier ('even church's') but is the adjective meaning smooth, CLEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight grip, as of a fist or jaw, is a firm hold.

clue.text: Unexpected first sign of break — game point following ace

indicators.note: the break's letter, game and point all follow the ace

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word break is used

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A tennis match turns suddenly: a break, then game point after an ace.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis terms set the scene; the game is rugby union, RU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sudden and without warning is unforeseen, as in a sudden halt.

clue.text: Daily points from all sides apparently taken literally

parts.note: the four compass points N, E, W and S cover all sides
apparently means on paper; taken literally, the compass points sit on a sheet of paper

explanation.surface: A daily paper offers views from every side, or so it seems, taken at its word.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'on paper' means apparently; 'taken literally', the compass points really are on a sheet, the second piece following the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a paper published every weekday, reporting current events.

clue.text: It's okay, not odd, to follow broadcast of knockout Big Bang episode?

indicators.note: the even letters follow the sound in the answer
broadcast means spoken on air, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: a cracker is a knockout, a stunner

indicators.note: not odd means even, so the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters are taken

explanation.surface: A TV episode about the Big Bang theory, said to be a smash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big Bang' suggests the universe's birth; here it is the 1883 volcanic explosion. CRACKER in a non-rhotic accent sounds like KRAKA.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1883 eruption of this Indonesian volcano was among the loudest explosions in recorded history.

clue.text: Heartless guy about to take the lead? Not Frank!

indicators.note: the abbreviation for 'about' is told to go in front, leading the rest

parts.note: CA is circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: the central letter of the word guy is removed, taking out its heart

parts.note: taken as written before its middle goes

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted man is about to take charge, and he is no open fellow named Frank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not Frank!' reads like a man's name being ruled out; it means 'not candid'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone guarded and evasive about their intentions is not open or candid.

clue.text: Commander capturing men having routed threat on southern peaks

indicators.note: the commander takes the men captive inside

parts.note: CBE is Commander of the Order of the British Empire
OR, other ranks, are the ordinary soldiers, the men

indicators.note: routed means cleared out, so only the outer letters of threat survive

explanation.surface: A commander takes his troops onto southern summits, the threat defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: These are Scottish hills between 2,500 and 3,000 feet, a step down from Munros.
explanation.definitionFit: These are a listed class of Scottish mountains, named after the climber who listed them.

clue.text: After two drinks, this setter's game!

indicators.note: the setter's word comes after the two drinks

parts.note: gin and rum are two drinks
the setter refers to himself, so his things are 'my'

explanation.surface: After a couple of drinks the setter is up for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like the adjective 'willing'; it is the noun, a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a card game for two in which players collect sets and runs.

clue.text: East End intellectuals reported some of their Boat Race?

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the result is said aloud and spelt as it sounds

parts.note: intellectuals are highbrows, and a Cockney from London's East End drops the H, saying 'ighbrows

explanation.surface: Cockney brainboxes talk about their part in the university rowing race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the Oxford-Cambridge rowing race, but in Cockney rhyming slang 'boat race' means face; 'their' ties the slang to the East Enders. Dropping the H from highbrows, 'East End' style, leaves a sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Brows are features of the face, so they are part of what rhyming slang calls the boat race.

clue.text: Borders on having succeeded after one month

indicators.note: the words 'on' and 'succeeded' come after the month in the answer

parts.note: APR is the short form of April, one month of the year
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone sits on the border, having made a success of things a month later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borders' looks like a verb; it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is an edging strip, such as the front of a stage or the paved border by a hangar.

clue.text: Dad stopping adult function after student drinks

indicators.note: the function comes after the student letter in the answer

parts.note: A is the film certificate for adult
L is the learner driver's plate, a student

indicators.note: Dad stops up the function, sitting in the middle of it like a plug

parts.note: cos, cosine, is a trigonometric function
pop is a word for dad

explanation.surface: Dad turns up to stop a grown-up party after the student drinking gets going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' suggests a party, which fits the drinking surface; here it is the maths function.
explanation.definitionFit: These are sweet, fizzy pre-mixed alcoholic beverages, often blamed for teenage drinking.

clue.text: Approach female upstart right away after taking the lead

indicators.note: the letter for right is sent away, taken out of the word
the leading letter is taken off the word

parts.note: a parvenue is a female upstart, a newly rich social climber

explanation.surface: An ambitious newcomer takes charge and promptly goes on the offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking the lead' removes the first letter, P, and 'right away' removes R.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a way of approach, especially a tree-lined drive leading to a house.

clue.text: Regularly expose busybody making money

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals: here every third letter of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone routinely unmasks a nosy neighbour and profits by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' usually means alternate letters; that gives nothing here, and every third letter of 'expose busybody' works.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the currency unit of Mexico and several other Latin American countries.

clue.text: Carelessly concedes kick on wing where props go in

indicators.note: done carelessly, the letters land in a jumbled order
a wing is a side, so a letter at the edge of kick is taken

explanation.surface: A rugby team gives away a free kick out wide, where the props go in for a scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby surface makes props forwards; they are stage props.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the space beside a theatre stage where scenery and props are stored.

clue.text: Heading off anguish, time running out for complaint

indicators.note: the letter for time runs out of the word, leaving it
the head, or first letter, of the word comes off

parts.note: heartache is anguish

explanation.surface: Someone heads off a crisis before the clock runs down on a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' means an ailment, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an ailment, and a pain in the ear is one.

clue.text: Girl eating peeled vegetable elicits comment in writing

indicators.note: the girl eats the trimmed vegetable, taking it inside her name

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

indicators.note: peeled means the skin, the outer letters, come off

parts.note: a potato is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A girl munching a peeled spud draws written remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peeled' removes the outer P and O.
explanation.definitionFit: To add notes in the margin of a text is to remark on it in writing.

clue.text: Singer from off-and-on screen embraced by performer

indicators.note: the performer wraps around the letters, holding them inside

parts.note: an actor is a performer

indicators.note: off and on means alternating letters, skipping the first, of screen

explanation.surface: A singer from the TV screen is hugged by a fellow star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' looks like a vocalist; it is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The dunnock or hedge sparrow belongs to this family of small songbirds.

clue.text: Endless pressure to go on pitch — captain may land you here

indicators.note: the pitch goes on after the shortened pressure
the last letter of the word for pressure is cut off

parts.note: heat means pressure, as in the heat is on
to pitch is to throw

explanation.surface: Constant pressure on the cricket pitch, where a captain might set you down.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket captain and pitch mislead; the captain flies a plane. Heathrow is London's main airport.
explanation.definitionFit: An airline captain lands passengers at an airport, and this is London's busiest.

clue.text: Middle-of-the-road guide to late-night events?

parts.note: a reflective stud set into the centre of a road guides drivers at night, and the phrase also suggests what a cat sees by on its nocturnal outings

explanation.surface: A guide to the night's entertainment that is neither edgy nor highbrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle-of-the-road' looks like 'unadventurous' but is literal: the studs sit in the centre of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: These glass reflectors set in road surfaces shine in headlights, guiding motorists after dark.

clue.text: Some mess I spill, ending up …

definitions.text: Some mess I spill, ending up …

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
some means a part of the words, so the letters are taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A clumsy confession trailing off mid-sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes SISPILLE from mesS I SPILL Ending, and 'up' turns it round. The trailing dots are what the clue's sentence ends with.
explanation.definitionFit: Three dots marking an omission or a trailing-off sentence, like those at the end of this clue.

clue.text: Compact, tense-free language

indicators.note: free of tense means the letter for tense is taken out

parts.note: terse means compact, brief
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A brief language with no verb tenses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' after 'tense-' looks like part of a compound adjective; it removes T.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Gaelic language of the Scottish Highlands or of Ireland.

clue.text: Test site cover-up on two levels

definitions.meaning: an atoll in the Marshall Islands where the US tested atomic bombs
a two-piece swimsuit covering the body at top and bottom

explanation.walkthrough: 'cover-up' suggests a scandal; it is swimwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-piece swimsuit was named after the atoll where nuclear tests had just made headlines.

clue.text: Angle to capture heart of pretty thing

indicators.note: the angling word captures the letters, holding them inside

parts.note: to angle is to fish

indicators.note: heart means the middle letters of the word pretty

explanation.surface: Fishing to land the core of a pretty object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thing' means an obsession, as in having a thing about shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a 'thing' about something means an obsessive fixation on it.

clue.text: Warning seen by abandoned Soviet group of planes?

parts.note: fore is the warning shouted on a golf course

indicators.note: abandoned means emptied, so only the outside letters of Soviet remain

explanation.surface: An alert goes out about a squadron of aircraft deserted by the Soviets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planes' looks like aircraft; here they are plane trees, the question mark showing a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood of plane trees is one kind of large area covered by trees.

clue.text: Repeatedly anger bishop about a problem overseas

indicators.note: repeatedly means the result is given twice over
about means turned around, read backwards

parts.note: ire is anger
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Someone keeps annoying a bishop about some trouble abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses IRE and B to give BERI, and 'Repeatedly' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: This vitamin B1 deficiency disease is found mainly in tropical countries, a health problem abroad.

clue.text: Uncovered urn in the style of an Attic feature?

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outer letters, so only the middle of the word urn is left

parts.note: after means in the style of, as in a painting after Rembrandt

explanation.surface: An urn unearthed in the manner of Greek pottery from Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attic' looks like the Athenian style that suits the urn; it is the loft, whose roof beams are a feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof beam is a structural feature you can see in an attic room.

clue.text: Intriguing topic is absorbing Left

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in, or absorb, the letter for left
intriguing means scheming, so these letters are plotted into a new order

explanation.surface: A fascinating subject that has the left wing hooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intriguing' rearranges TOPIC IS and 'absorbing' puts L inside. Read whole, the clue describes the subject: scheming, a hot topic, consuming the Left.
explanation.definitionFit: Party scheming and the contests of left and right are the stuff of government affairs.

clue.text: Fruit seed radius

parts.note: a pea is a seed in a pod
R is the abbreviation for radius in geometry

explanation.surface: A list of fruit parts: the seed, and the distance across.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the sweet, juicy tree fruit narrowing towards the stalk.

clue.text: The kings we blessed five times out of seven?

indicators.note: blessed is a polite word for blasted, damned, so the letters are blasted into a new order

explanation.surface: Kings who claim divine favour most evenings of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blessed' reads as holy; it is a mild curse word standing for 'wrecked'.
explanation.definitionFit: Monday to Friday evenings are five of the week's seven nights.
